First, what is a program? Tower of Hanoi

    

    
hanoi-r.c

    
Can you write it without recursion?

    
Asked in an OS class: no hand went up

    
Yes: keep your own array of frames, plus a loopa running program is a stack of frames; a call just pushes one more

    
Evanherk, GFDL / CC BY-SA 3.0 · Code: hanoi-r.c by Yanyan Jiang (jyywiki.cn/OS/demos/intro/hanoi-nr)

  

  

    
A program = a stack of frames, each with its own PC

    
    

    
STACK (top = running)

    

    

    
No magic in recursion: the CPU's call and ret do exactly this

    
After hanoi-nr.c by Yanyan Jiang (jyywiki.cn/OS/demos/intro/hanoi-nr)

no C library, no main

argc

strace: watch every system call

    
terminal

    
3

    
$ strace ./hello (the C version)

    

    
35

    

      load libc19set up9printf buffer4our write1exit1
    

    
execve is the 1st · the one line we asked for is the 34th

    
printf is not magic: in the end, it is one write system call

    
Traced on Ubuntu 24.04 (gcc 13, glibc 2.39); counts differ a little between systems

  

  

    
How many system calls? One dot = one call

    
    

    
gcc is 5 programsgcc · cc1 · as · collect2 · ld

    
Big or small, every program keeps asking the OS

    
Counted with a small ptrace tool that follows child processes, like strace -f · Ubuntu 24.04, gcc 13, glibc 2.39, Python 3.12

How does a window app draw?

    

      

      
      

      

      

      

      

    

    
Keys and clicks → eventsthe app reads them from a socket

    
Pictures → draw requeststhe app writes them to the display server

    
The app never touches the screenonly the server does · Wayland today: the same idea

    
Any app, even one with windows, is computation plus system calls

    
David Gerard (original), recreated by Efitu, CC BY-SA 3.0 · After Yanyan Jiang's strace xedit demo

  

  

    

    

    
The OS manages many state machines

    

    
operating system

    
Each one: computation + system calls

    
The OS decides who runs next

    
Every app asks the same OS, and waits its turn for the CPUthat is the OS seen from the application side

    
Ximeg, CC BY-SA 3.0

  

  

    
The CPU does not know there is an OS

    
Intel 80386a machine that runs instructions

    
fetch the instruction at PC → execute → repeat

    

    

    
▲ PC

    
OS: interrupt handler

    
eb fe = jmp . (jump to itself): stuck forever?

    
No. An interrupt is the way outthe CPU jumps to code the OS set up

    

    
An endless loop cannot freeze your laptopthe timer interrupt gives the CPU back to the OS

    
Pauli Rautakorpi, CC BY 3.0 · 16-bit x86 encodings · After Yanyan Jiang, NJU OS 2026

  

  

    
Power on: where does the CPU start?

    

    

    
reset

    
x86 CPU right after reset

      

        
CS
F000
base FFFF0000

        
IP
FFF0

        
EFLAGS
00000002
interrupts off

        
CR0
60000010
real mode, no paging

      

    
first fetch → 0xFFFFFFF0

    
16 bytes below 4 GB

    
RISC-V in QEMU (virt): pc = 0x1000every CPU has a fixed reset state, chosen by its designers

    
Reset is the first state of the hardware state machine. No OS yet.

    
Gerolsteiner91 (Niklas Bildhauer), CC BY-SA 2.5 · Values: Intel SDM Vol. 3A, processor state after reset · QEMU virt machine

1998

    
The CIH virusspread through Windows 95 and 98 programs

    
April 26: it rewrote
the BIOS chipthe PC could not start again

    
Fix: replace or reprogram
the chiptoday: firmware updates must be signed

    
If the first program is broken, nothing else can startthis is why the boot chain matters for security

    
Tremaster, CC BY-SA 3.0

  

  

    

    

    
IBM PC · master boot recordSector 0: 512 bytes that end in 55 AA

    

      
boot code446 bytes

      
partition table64 bytes

      
55 AA2 bytes

    

    
MEMORY
0x7C00

    
The firmware copies it to 0x7C00 and jumps there

    
446 bytes: just enough code to load a bigger loaderGRUB starts here, then loads the kernel

    
BIOS or UEFI: the firmware just loads the next programUEFI reads a boot file from a special partition instead

    
Matthew Field (Mfield), CC BY-SA 3.0 · Layout after Yanyan Jiang, NJU OS 2026
